question:
The contribution made by each sector of the economy into GDP is called ______.

[SSC GD 2022]
options: nominal composition
real composition
real GDP
structural composition
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is structural composition

Explanation:
The structural composition refers to the contribution made by each sector of the economy (primary, secondary, and tertiary) to the GDP. It reflects the economic structure and the relative importance of different sectors. For example, in developing countries, the primary sector (agriculture) contributes more, while in developed economies, the tertiary sector (services) dominates. Understanding structural composition helps in policy-making and resource allocation for balanced economic growth.

Extra Facts:
GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a year. It is categorized into three sectors: primary (agriculture), secondary (industry), and tertiary (services). The structural composition shows the percentage contribution of each sector to GDP, indicating the stage of economic development. For instance, a higher share of services suggests a more advanced economy.

question_hi:
अर्थव्यवस्था के प्रत्येक क्षेत्रक द्वारा GDP में किए गए योगदान से ही ______________ तैयार होता है।

[SSC GD 2022]
options_hi: नाममात्र रचना
वास्तविक ढांचा
वास्तविक GDP
सांकेतिक ढांचा
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है सांकेतिक ढांचा

Explanation:
सांकेतिक ढांचा (Structural Composition) अर्थव्यवस्था के विभिन्न क्षेत्रकों जैसे कृषि, उद्योग और सेवा क्षेत्र द्वारा GDP में किए गए योगदान को दर्शाता है। यह अर्थव्यवस्था की संरचना और विभिन्न क्षेत्रों के महत्व को समझने में मदद करता है। उदाहरण के लिए, विकासशील देशों में कृषि क्षेत्र का योगदान अधिक होता है, जबकि विकसित देशों में सेवा क्षेत्र का। यह आर्थिक नीतियों को बनाने और संसाधनों के आवंटन में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है।

Extra Facts:
GDP (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद) एक वर्ष में देश की सीमा के भीतर उत्पादित सभी अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का कुल मूल्य है। इसे तीन प्रमुख क्षेत्रों - प्राथमिक (कृषि), द्वितीयक (उद्योग) और तृतीयक (सेवा) में विभाजित किया जा सकता है। सांकेतिक ढांचा इन क्षेत्रों के योगदान को प्रतिशत के रूप में दर्शाता है और आर्थिक विकास के स्तर को समझने में मदद करता है।

question:
Value of wheat in flour is a part of____________ method of measurement of its national income.

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: income
circular income
expenditure
value added
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is value added

Explanation:
The 'Value Added Method' of measuring national income calculates the value added at each stage of production. The value of wheat in flour is part of this method because it represents the value added during the process of converting wheat into flour. In this method, the value of intermediate goods is subtracted from the final product's value to compute 'value addition.' This approach avoids the problem of double counting and clarifies the contribution of different sectors to the economy.

Extra Facts:
The three main methods of measuring national income are: Income Method (total factor income), Production Method (value added), and Expenditure Method (total final expenditure). The value-added method separately measures contributions from primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors. It is particularly useful for GDP calculation as it reflects productivity at different economic levels.

☛ Which method faces double counting issues? → Production Method (if not value-added)
☛ What is NDP? → GDP - Depreciation
☛ What is included in factor income? → Wages, Interest, Profit, Rent
question_hi:
आटे में गेहूँ का मूल्य इसकी राष्ट्रीय आय के मापन की__________ विधि का एक भाग है।

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options_hi: आय
चक्रीय आय
व्यय
मूल्यवर्धित
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है मूल्यवर्धित

Explanation:
राष्ट्रीय आय की गणना की 'मूल्यवर्धित विधि' (Value Added Method) में, प्रत्येक उत्पादन चरण में जोड़े गए मूल्य को मापा जाता है। आटे में गेहूँ का मूल्य इस विधि का एक भाग है क्योंकि यह गेहूँ से आटा बनाने की प्रक्रिया में जोड़ा गया मूल्य दर्शाता है। इस विधि में, अंतिम उत्पाद के मूल्य से मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं के मूल्य को घटाकर 'मूल्यवर्धन' की गणना की जाती है। यह विधि दोहरी गणना (Double Counting) की समस्या से बचाती है और अर्थव्यवस्था के विभिन्न क्षेत्रों में उत्पादन के योगदान को स्पष्ट करती है।

Extra Facts:
राष्ट्रीय आय मापन की तीन मुख्य विधियाँ हैं: आय विधि (कुल कारक आय), उत्पादन विधि (मूल्यवर्धित), और व्यय विधि (कुल अंतिम व्यय)। मूल्यवर्धित विधि में, प्राथमिक, द्वितीयक और तृतीयक क्षेत्रों के योगदान को अलग-अलग मापा जाता है। यह विधि GDP (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद) की गणना के लिए विशेष रूप से उपयोगी है, क्योंकि यह अर्थव्यवस्था के विभिन्न स्तरों पर उत्पादकता को दर्शाती है।

question:
Final goods are divided into:

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: raw materials and semi-finished goods
single goods and composite goods
consumption goods and capital goods
War goods and civilian goods
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is consumption goods and capital goods

Explanation:
Final goods are those goods that are ready for final use and are not used in any further production process. They are divided into two categories: consumption goods and capital goods. Consumption goods directly satisfy consumer needs, such as food, clothing, etc. On the other hand, capital goods are used in the production process and enhance future production capacity, such as machinery, equipment, etc. This classification is crucial for calculating national income and economic analysis.

Extra Facts:
It is essential to understand the difference between final goods and intermediate goods. Intermediate goods are used in the production process and become part of final goods. For example, flour used to make bread is an intermediate good, while bread is a final good. In national income calculation, only the value of final goods is included to avoid double counting.

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :

☛ What are intermediate goods? → Goods used in the production process
☛ Whose value is included in national income? → Only final goods
☛ What is double counting? → Adding the value of both intermediate and final goods
☛ What are capital goods? → Goods that enhance future production capacity
question_hi:
अंतिम वस्तुएँ कितने वर्गों में विभाजित होती हैं?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options_hi: कच्चा माल और अर्ध-निर्मित वस्तुएँ
एकल वस्तुएँ और मिश्रित वस्तुएँ
उपभोग वस्तुएं और पूंजीगत वस्तुएं
युद्ध वस्तुएँ और नागरिक वस्तुएँ
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है उपभोग वस्तुएं और पूंजीगत वस्तुएं

Explanation:
अंतिम वस्तुएँ वे वस्तुएँ होती हैं जो अंतिम उपयोग के लिए तैयार होती हैं और इन्हें आगे किसी उत्पादन प्रक्रिया में उपयोग नहीं किया जाता है। ये दो प्रकार की होती हैं: उपभोग वस्तुएं और पूंजीगत वस्तुएं। उपभोग वस्तुएं सीधे उपभोक्ताओं की आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करती हैं, जैसे कि भोजन, कपड़े आदि। दूसरी ओर, पूंजीगत वस्तुएं उत्पादन प्रक्रिया में उपयोग की जाती हैं और भविष्य में उत्पादन करने की क्षमता बढ़ाती हैं, जैसे कि मशीनें, उपकरण आदि। यह वर्गीकरण राष्ट्रीय आय की गणना और आर्थिक विश्लेषण में महत्वपूर्ण है।

Extra Facts:
अंतिम वस्तुओं और मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं के बीच अंतर समझना आवश्यक है। मध्यवर्ती वस्तुएं उत्पादन प्रक्रिया में उपयोग की जाती हैं और अंतिम वस्तुओं में शामिल हो जाती हैं। उदाहरण के लिए, आटा जो ब्रेड बनाने में उपयोग किया जाता है, एक मध्यवर्ती वस्तु है, जबकि ब्रेड एक अंतिम वस्तु है। राष्ट्रीय आय की गणना में केवल अंतिम वस्तुओं का मूल्य शामिल किया जाता है ताकि दोहरी गणना से बचा जा सके।

question:
Deduction of depreciation from Gross National Product is known as:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Net National Product
Gross Domestic Product
National Income
Corporate Tax
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Net National Product

Explanation:
The deduction of depreciation from Gross National Product (GNP) is known as Net National Product (NNP). Depreciation represents the wear and tear of capital goods over time. NNP reflects the true productive capacity of an economy by accounting for capital consumption. The formula for NNP is:
NNP = GNP – Depreciation

Extra Facts:
GNP measures the total market value of all final goods and services produced by a country's residents, regardless of production location. In contrast, GDP only considers production within a country's geographical boundaries. NNP is a 'net' version of GNP, indicating sustainable economic output. It is crucial for assessing long-term growth potential.

☛ How is National Income calculated? → NNP at Factor Cost
☛ What is Depreciation? → Decline in value of capital assets
☛ Formula of NNP? → GNP – Depreciation
☛ Who calculates National Income in India? → CSO (Central Statistical Office)
question_hi:
सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद से मूल्यह्रास की कटौती के रूप में जाना जाता है

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: शुद्ध राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद
सकल घरेलु उत्पाद
राष्ट्रीय आय
निगम कर
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है शुद्ध राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद

Explanation:
सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (GNP) से मूल्यह्रास (Depreciation) की कटौती के बाद प्राप्त मूल्य को 'शुद्ध राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद' (Net National Product - NNP) कहा जाता है। मूल्यह्रास, पूंजीगत वस्तुओं के उपयोग और समय के साथ होने वाले मूल्य में कमी को दर्शाता है। यह एक महत्वपूर्ण आर्थिक संकेतक है जो देश की वास्तविक आर्थिक उत्पादकता को दर्शाता है, क्योंकि इसमें पूंजी के 'घिसावट' को समायोजित किया जाता है। NNP की गणना निम्न सूत्र द्वारा की जाती है:
NNP = GNP - मूल्यह्रास

Extra Facts:
GNP एक देश के नागरिकों द्वारा उत्पादित सभी अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का बाजार मूल्य है, चाहे उत्पादन देश के अंदर या बाहर किया गया हो। वहीं, GDP केवल देश की भौगोलिक सीमा के अंदर उत्पादित वस्तुओं और सेवाओं को मापता है। NNP, GNP का एक 'शुद्ध' संस्करण है जो अर्थव्यवस्था की टिकाऊ उत्पादन क्षमता को दर्शाता है।

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :

☛ राष्ट्रीय आय की गणना कैसे की जाती है? → NNP at Factor Cost
☛ मूल्यह्रास क्या होता है? → पूंजीगत वस्तुओं के मूल्य में कमी

question:
Which of these is the correct reason for a goods to be identified as a final goods

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: It is not processed by a consumer after purchase.
It cannot be recycled or re-used.
It is in the last stage of the product life cycle.
It is not processed further by a producer
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It is not processed further by a producer.

Explanation:
A final good is a product that is not processed further by a producer and is ready for direct use by the consumer. It is distinct from intermediate goods, which undergo further processing in the production process. The value of final goods is included in national income, whereas intermediate goods are not. For example, bread bought by a consumer is a final good, but the flour used to make the bread is an intermediate good.

Extra Facts:
Final goods can be categorized into two types: consumer goods (e.g., food, clothing) and capital goods (e.g., machinery, buildings). The valuation of final goods is done at market prices and directly contributes to national income calculation. Intermediate goods are not valued separately to avoid the problem of double-counting.

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ What is an intermediate good? → A good that undergoes further processing in production
☛ Which good's value is included in national income? → Final good
☛ What is an example of a capital good? → Machinery
☛ What is an example of a consumer good? → Bread
☛ What problem is associated with double-counting? → Intermediate goods

Explanation:
अंतिम वस्तु वह वस्तु है जिसे निर्माता द्वारा आगे संसाधित नहीं किया जाता है और जो सीधे उपभोक्ता द्वारा उपयोग के लिए तैयार होती है। यह मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं से अलग होती है, जिन्हें उत्पादन प्रक्रिया में आगे संसाधित किया जाता है। अंतिम वस्तु का मूल्य राष्ट्रीय आय में शामिल किया जाता है, जबकि मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं का नहीं। उदाहरण के लिए, एक ब्रेड जो उपभोक्ता द्वारा खरीदी जाती है, अंतिम वस्तु है, लेकिन आटा जिससे ब्रेड बनाई जाती है, मध्यवर्ती वस्तु है।

Extra Facts:
अंतिम वस्तुओं को दो श्रेणियों में बांटा जा सकता है: उपभोक्ता वस्तुएं (जैसे कि भोजन, कपड़े) और पूंजीगत वस्तुएं (जैसे कि मशीनें, इमारतें)। अंतिम वस्तुओं का मूल्यांकन बाजार मूल्य पर किया जाता है और यह सीधे राष्ट्रीय आय गणना में जुड़ता है। मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं का मूल्यांकन नहीं किया जाता क्योंकि इससे दोहरी गणना की समस्या उत्पन्न होती है।

question:
Which of the following is correct regarding Personal Disposable Income?

[SSC GD 2022]
options: Personal Disposable Income ≡ Personal Income + Personal tax payments – Non-tax payments
Personal Disposable Income ≡ Personal Income – Personal tax payments + Non-tax payments
Personal Disposable Income ≡ Personal Income + Personal tax payments + Non-tax payments
Personal Disposable Income ≡ Personal Income – Personal tax payments – Non-tax payments
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Personal Disposable Income ≡ Personal Income – Personal tax payments – Non-tax payments

Explanation:
Personal Disposable Income (PDI) is the income available to individuals for consumption and saving after deducting personal tax payments and non-tax payments from personal income. Non-tax payments include fines, court fees, social security contributions, etc. This formula is a crucial part of national income accounting in economics and indicates the actual income individuals have left to spend or save. It reflects the financial health of households and their capacity to contribute to economic demand.

Extra Facts:
PDI is used to analyze consumption and savings patterns in an economy. It plays a vital role in determining the level of demand. Higher PDI can lead to increased consumption and savings, while higher tax and non-tax payments reduce PDI, negatively impacting economic activity. Governments use fiscal policies to influence PDI through taxation and subsidies. Understanding PDI helps in formulating policies to boost economic growth and stability.

[SSC GD 2022]
options_hi: व्यक्तिगत प्रयोज्य आय ≡ व्यक्तिगत आय + व्यक्तिगत कर अदायगी - गैर-कर अदायगी

व्यक्तिगत प्रयोज्य आय ≡ व्यक्तिगत आय – व्यक्तिगत कर अदायगी – गैर-कर अदायगी
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है व्यक्तिगत प्रयोज्य आय ≡ व्यक्तिगत आय – व्यक्तिगत कर अदायगी – गैर-कर अदायगी

Explanation:
व्यक्तिगत प्रयोज्य आय (Personal Disposable Income - PDI) वह आय है जो व्यक्तियों के पास उपभोग और बचत के लिए उपलब्ध होती है। यह व्यक्तिगत आय (Personal Income) से व्यक्तिगत कर अदायगी (Personal Tax Payments) और गैर-कर अदायगी (Non-tax Payments) को घटाकर प्राप्त की जाती है। इसमें गैर-कर अदायगी जैसे जुर्माना, अदालती फीस, सामाजिक सुरक्षा योगदान आदि शामिल होते हैं। यह सूत्र अर्थशास्त्र में राष्ट्रीय आय लेखांकन का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा है और यह दर्शाता है कि व्यक्तियों के पास वास्तव में कितनी आय खर्च करने के लिए बचती है।

Extra Facts:
व्यक्तिगत प्रयोज्य आय का उपयोग उपभोग और बचत के विश्लेषण के लिए किया जाता है। यह अर्थव्यवस्था में मांग के स्तर को निर्धारित करने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाती है। यदि PDI अधिक होती है, तो उपभोग और बचत दोनों बढ़ सकते हैं। इसके विपरीत, यदि कर और गैर-कर अदायगी अधिक होती है, तो PDI कम हो जाती है, जिससे उपभोग और बचत पर नकारात्मक प्रभाव पड़ सकता है। यह आर्थिक नीति निर्माण में भी महत्वपूर्ण है, क्योंकि सरकार कर और गैर-कर राजस्व के माध्यम से PDI को प्रभावित कर सकती है।

question:
What is net investment?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Sum of all the investments in a country
Gross investment + depreciation
Gross capital investment - indirect taxes
Gross investment - depreciation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gross investment - depreciation

Explanation:
Net investment refers to the amount obtained by subtracting depreciation from gross investment. Depreciation represents the wear and tear or decline in the value of capital goods over time. Net investment indicates the actual capital formation in an economy, while gross investment includes both new capital formation and replacement of existing capital stock. It is a crucial indicator for measuring real economic growth.

Extra Facts:
Gross investment includes both the creation of new capital goods and the replacement of existing capital stock. Depreciation accounts for the reduction in the value of capital goods due to usage and obsolescence. Net investment reflects the real increase in an economy's productive capacity. It is an essential component in national income accounting.

☛ What is depreciation? → Decline in the value of capital goods

☛ How is net investment calculated? → Gross investment - depreciation

शुद्ध निवेश क्या है?

सकल पूंजी निवेश - अप्रत्यक्ष कर

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है सकल निवेश - मूल्यह्रास

Explanation:
शुद्ध निवेश का अर्थ है किसी अर्थव्यवस्था में सकल निवेश में से मूल्यह्रास (Depreciation) को घटाकर प्राप्त की गई राशि। मूल्यह्रास पूंजीगत वस्तुओं के उपयोग और समय के साथ होने वाले मूल्य में कमी को दर्शाता है। शुद्ध निवेश वास्तविक पूंजी निर्माण को दर्शाता है, जबकि सकल निवेश में मूल्यह्रास भी शामिल होता है। यह अर्थव्यवस्था की वास्तविक वृद्धि को मापने का एक महत्वपूर्ण सूचक है।

Extra Facts:
सकल निवेश में नई पूंजीगत वस्तुओं के निर्माण और मौजूदा पूंजी स्टॉक के प्रतिस्थापन दोनों शामिल होते हैं। मूल्यह्रास पूंजीगत वस्तुओं के टूट-फूट और पुराने होने के कारण उनके मूल्य में होने वाली कमी को दर्शाता है। शुद्ध निवेश अर्थव्यवस्था की उत्पादन क्षमता में वास्तविक वृद्धि को दर्शाता है। यह राष्ट्रीय आय गणना में एक महत्वपूर्ण घटक है।

question:
Goods such as food, clothing and services such as recreation that are consumed when purchased by their ultimate consumers are called

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Consumption goods
Final goods
Capital goods
Intermediate goods
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Consumption goods

Explanation:
Consumption goods are products and services like food, clothing, and recreation that are directly consumed by end-users. These goods are not used for further production or processing but satisfy immediate consumer needs. While they can be termed as 'final goods', 'consumption goods' specifically refer to items bought for personal use. 'Capital goods' (e.g., machinery) and 'intermediate goods' (e.g., raw materials) are used in production processes, not for direct consumption.

Extra Facts:
Consumption goods are categorized into durable (e.g., cars, appliances) and non-durable (e.g., groceries). Their value is included in GDP calculations as they represent final demand. Consumer spending is a major component of aggregate demand, influencing economic growth. Demand for these goods depends on income levels, prices, and consumer preferences. Keynesian economics emphasizes their role in driving economic cycles.

☛ Goods used in production processes are termed? → Intermediate goods
☛ What are goods like machinery classified as? → Capital goods
☛ Which goods are included in GDP calculations? → Final goods
☛ What category do smartphones and furniture fall under? → Durable consumption goods

Explanation:
उपभोग वस्तुएँ वे वस्तुएँ और सेवाएँ हैं जिन्हें अंतिम उपभोक्ता द्वारा सीधे उपभोग किया जाता है, जैसे भोजन, कपड़े और मनोरंजन। ये वस्तुएँ उत्पादन प्रक्रिया में और प्रसंस्करण के लिए उपयोग नहीं की जाती हैं, बल्कि सीधे उपभोक्ता की आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करती हैं। इन्हें 'अंतिम माल' भी कहा जा सकता है, लेकिन 'उपभोग वस्तुएँ' शब्द विशेष रूप से उन वस्तुओं को संदर्भित करता है जो उपभोग के लिए खरीदी जाती हैं। 'पूंजीगत वस्तुएं' और 'मध्यवर्ती माल' उत्पादन प्रक्रिया में उपयोग की जाती हैं, न कि सीधे उपभोग के लिए।

question:
Which term is used to denote the mean income computed for every man, woman, and child in a particular group including those living in group quarters?

[SSC GD 2024]
options: Per capita income
Per hundred income
GDP
PRCS
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Per capita income

Explanation:
Per capita income is an economic measure that represents the average income earned per person (men, women, and children) in a specific group (e.g., country, state, city), including those living in group quarters. It is a key indicator of economic development and living standards. Per capita income is calculated by dividing the total national income by the total population. This metric helps in understanding the 'overall economic performance' and 'income distribution' of an economy.

Extra Facts:
Apart from per capita income, other important economic indicators include Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Gross National Product (GNP), and Human Development Index (HDI). GDP measures the total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders, while GNP includes the income earned by a country's citizens both domestically and abroad. HDI measures health, education, and income levels to assess human development.

☛ What does Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measure? → Total value of goods and services produced within a country
☛ What factors does the Human Development Index (HDI) consider? → Health, education, income
☛ What is the difference between GNP and GDP? → GNP includes income earned by citizens abroad
☛ What is the most common measure of economic growth? → GDP growth rate

प्रति व्यक्ति आय के अलावा, अन्य महत्वपूर्ण आर्थिक संकेतकों में सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP), सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (GNP), और मानव विकास सूचकांक (HDI) शामिल हैं। GDP किसी देश की सीमा के भीतर उत्पादित सभी वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का कुल मूल्य है, जबकि GNP देश के नागरिकों द्वारा देश के अंदर और बाहर उत्पादित सभी वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का मूल्य है। HDI स्वास्थ्य, शिक्षा और आय के स्तर को मापता है।

question:
GDP calculated at some constant set of prices is called___________.

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: real GDP
domestic GDP
current GDP
nominal GDP
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is real GDP

Explanation:
Real GDP is calculated using the prices of a fixed base year, eliminating the effects of inflation or deflation. It reflects the actual growth of an economy by measuring changes in the quantity of output rather than price fluctuations. Also known as 'GDP at constant prices', it provides a more accurate comparison for economic analysis over time.

Extra Facts:
Nominal GDP is measured at current market prices and is influenced by inflation. The GDP deflator measures inflation by comparing real and nominal GDP. The base year is periodically updated to incorporate recent price trends in GDP calculations.

question:
The aggregate value of goods and services produced in an economy can be calculated by three methods: income method, expenditure method and ______ method.

[SSC CGL 2019]
options: spending
product / value added
deposit
lending
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is product / value added

Explanation:
The aggregate value of goods and services produced in an economy is calculated using three primary methods: income method (sum of incomes generated in production), expenditure method (total spending on final goods and services), and product / value-added method (sum of value added at each production stage). The 'value-added method' avoids double-counting of intermediate goods by summing the incremental value contributed at each stage of production, making it a reliable measure of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

Extra Facts:
GDP is a key indicator of a country's economic activity. The income method includes wages, profits, interest, and rent, while the expenditure method covers consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports. The value-added method measures the value added at different production stages, such as raw materials to finished goods. This method helps analyze the contribution of various sectors to the economy.

☛ What is included in the income method? → Wages, profits, interest, rent
☛ What is included in the expenditure method? → Consumption, investment, government spending, net exports
☛ What is the full form of GDP? → Gross Domestic Product

question:
While estimating Gross Domestic Product, the monetary value of only final goods are considered because ___________.
a. its immobility, the active economic flow is ended.
b. of the issues of double counting
c. the value added at each stage of the production process is included

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Only b
Only a
All a, b and c
Only b and c
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Only b and c

Explanation:
While estimating Gross Domestic Product (GDP), only the monetary value of final goods is considered because including intermediate goods leads to the problem of double counting. For example, if flour and wheat are both included in the production of bread, their values would be counted multiple times, leading to an overestimation of GDP. Additionally, GDP calculation uses the value-added method, where only the value added at each stage of production is included. This avoids double counting and ensures an accurate estimation of GDP.

Extra Facts:
There are three main methods to calculate GDP: Production Approach, Income Approach, and Expenditure Approach. All these methods consider only the value of final goods and services. In the value-added method, the value added by each firm (output minus intermediate consumption) is included in GDP. This method also highlights the contribution of different sectors of the economy.

question:
____________ ≡ Sum total of gross value added of all the firms in the economy

[SSC GD 2022]
options: GDP
GNP
NI
NNP
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is GDP (Gross Domestic Product)

Explanation:
GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period. It is calculated using the value-added approach, where the value added at each stage of production is summed up. The formula GDP ≡ Σ (Gross Value Added by all firms) represents this method. GDP is a key indicator of economic size and growth. Other options like GNP, NI, and NNP are based on different concepts, involving factors like net income from abroad or depreciation.

Extra Facts:
GDP can be calculated using three methods: Production (Value Added), Income, and Expenditure approaches. The Value Added Method sums up the value added by each sector (agriculture, industry, services). GDP includes only final goods and services, excluding intermediate goods. It measures output produced within a country’s borders, regardless of the producer’s nationality.

question:
Calculate the GDP at factor cost given in the following data.
GDP at market price = 600 crores
Consumption of fixed capital = 100 crores
Indirect taxes = 200 crores
Subsidies = 50 crores

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: 850 crores
450 crores
950 crores
350 crores
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 450 crores

Explanation:
GDP at factor cost is calculated by subtracting indirect taxes and adding subsidies to GDP at market price. Consumption of fixed capital is not included in this calculation as it is not part of GDP at factor cost. The formula is:
GDP at Factor Cost = GDP at Market Price - Indirect Taxes + Subsidies
= 600 crores - 200 crores + 50 crores
= 450 crores

Extra Facts:
GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period. GDP at factor cost represents payments made to factors of production, whereas GDP at market price includes indirect taxes and subsidies. Indirect taxes are levied by the government on goods and services, while subsidies are financial assistance given to producers.

question:
Which of the following elements is NOT included in the circular flow of Income in a simple economy?

[NTPC CBT 2]
options: Factory
Goods and services
Depreciation
Spending
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Depreciation

Explanation:
In a simple economy, the circular flow of income involves two main sectors - Households and Firms. It includes Goods and Services and Spending. Factory is part of the firm and hence included. However, Depreciation is not part of the circular flow as it represents the decline in the value of capital assets, not the flow of income or expenditure. It is a non-cash transaction included in national income accounting but not in the basic circular flow model.

Extra Facts:
The Circular Flow of Income Model provides a basic framework to understand the flow of money and resources in an economy. It includes Real Flow (Goods and Services) and Monetary Flow (Payments). A Simple Economy does not include the government and foreign sectors. Including Depreciation makes it an expanded model, termed an open economy.

question:
The_____ of a firm during a year ≡ production of the firm during the year — sale of the firm during the year.

[SSC GD 2024]
options: opening stock
change in inventories and working capitals
closing stock
change of inventories
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is change in inventories

Explanation:
The change in inventories refers to the difference between the goods produced by a firm and the goods sold during a year. If production exceeds sales, inventories increase, and if sales exceed production, inventories decrease. This is a crucial concept in national income accounting as it reflects the unplanned accumulation or depletion of stocks. The formula is:
Change in Inventories = Production – Sales

Extra Facts:
- Change in inventories is also called unplanned inventory investment.
- An increase in inventories indicates lower-than-expected sales, while a decrease suggests higher sales than production.
- It plays a key role in determining a firm’s financial health and macroeconomic stability.

माल-सूची में परिवर्तन = उत्पादन – बिक्री

question:
What is the value of investment multiplier when MPC = MPS?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 1
2
infinite
10
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2

Explanation:
When MPC (Marginal Propensity to Consume) = MPS (Marginal Propensity to Save), both values are 0.5 because MPC + MPS = 1. The investment multiplier (K) is calculated using the formula K = 1 / MPS or K = 1 / (1 - MPC). If MPC = MPS = 0.5, then K = 1 / 0.5 = 2. The investment multiplier represents the change in income resulting from a change in investment in the economy. It is a key concept in Keynesian economics that helps determine the level of income and employment.

Extra Facts:
Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) is the proportion of incremental income spent on consumption, while Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS) is the proportion saved. MPC + MPS always equals 1. The value of the investment multiplier is directly proportional to MPC; the higher the MPC, the higher the multiplier. This concept plays a crucial role in determining national income.

☛ What is the formula for the investment multiplier? → K = 1 / MPS

☛ What does the investment multiplier indicate in Keynesian economics? → Change in income
☛ What is the investment multiplier at full employment? → Zero

question:
Which of the following is NOT correct regarding circular flow of income?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Savings as well as government expenditure are injections to the circular flow
The income of one sector becomes the expenditure of the other.
In a circular flow, leakages are equal to injections.
The real flow and monetary flow move in a circular manner in an opposite direction.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is " Savings as well as government expenditure are injections to the circular flow."

Explanation:
In the circular flow of income, 'injections' are elements that increase the flow of money in the economy, such as 'investment (I), government expenditure (G), and exports (X)'. On the other hand, 'savings (S)' are a 'leakage' because they reduce the flow of income. Therefore, the statement that both savings and government expenditure are injections is incorrect. Government expenditure is an injection, but savings are not. The other options are correct: income from one sector becomes the expenditure of another, leakages equal injections, and real flow (goods and services) and monetary flow (money) move in opposite directions.

Extra Facts:
The circular flow model illustrates the relationship between income, expenditure, and production in an economy. It consists of two types of flows: real flow (goods and services) and monetary flow (money). This model shows the exchange between households, firms, government, and the foreign sector. When leakages (savings, taxes, imports) and injections (investment, government spending, exports) are balanced, the economy remains stable. This model also helps in calculating national income.

आय के चक्रीय प्रवाह में, 'अंत:क्षेपण (injections)' वे तत्व हैं जो अर्थव्यवस्था में धन के प्रवाह को बढ़ाते हैं, जैसे 'निवेश (I), सरकारी व्यय (G), और निर्यात (X)'। दूसरी ओर, 'बचत (S)' एक 'क्षरण (leakage)' है क्योंकि यह आय के प्रवाह को कम करती है। इसलिए, यह कथन गलत है कि बचत और सरकारी व्यय दोनों अंत:क्षेपण हैं। सरकारी व्यय अंत:क्षेपण है, लेकिन बचत नहीं। अन्य विकल्प सही हैं: आय का एक क्षेत्र से दूसरे क्षेत्र में स्थानांतरण होता है, क्षरण और अंत:क्षेपण संतुलित होते हैं, और वास्तविक प्रवाह (वस्तुएं और सेवाएं) तथा मौद्रिक प्रवाह (धन) विपरीत दिशाओं में चलते हैं।

Extra Facts:
चक्रीय प्रवाह मॉडल अर्थव्यवस्था में आय, व्यय और उत्पादन के बीच संबंध को दर्शाता है। इसमें दो प्रकार के प्रवाह होते हैं: वास्तविक प्रवाह (वस्तुएं और सेवाएं) और मौद्रिक प्रवाह (धन)। यह मॉडल परिवारों, फर्मों, सरकार और विदेशी क्षेत्र के बीच आदान-प्रदान को दर्शाता है। क्षरण (leakages) (बचत, कर, आयात) और अंत:क्षेपण (injections) (निवेश, सरकारी व्यय, निर्यात) संतुलन में होने पर अर्थव्यवस्था स्थिर रहती है। यह मॉडल राष्ट्रीय आय की गणना में भी मदद करता है।

question:
The Gross Domestic Product of a country is derived from the different sectors of the economy, namely _______.

[SSC GD 2024]
options: commercial and trading sector
rural and urban sectors
agricultural sector, and the industrial sector only
agricultural sector, the industrial sector and the service sector
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is agricultural sector, the industrial sector and the service sector

Explanation:
The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of a country is derived from its three major economic sectors - agriculture, industry, and services. These sectors collectively represent the total economic activities of a nation. The agricultural sector includes crop production, livestock, and forestry. The industrial sector comprises manufacturing, mining, and construction, while the service sector includes activities like banking, education, healthcare, and tourism. GDP is calculated by considering the contributions of all three sectors, reflecting the economic growth and development of the country.

Extra Facts:
GDP can be calculated using three methods - production, income, and expenditure approaches. In India, the service sector contributes the most to GDP, accounting for over 50%. The agricultural sector's contribution has declined to around 15-20%, while the industrial sector contributes approximately 25-30%. The GDP growth rate is a crucial indicator of an economy's health.

☛ Which sector contributes the most to India's GDP? → Service Sector
☛ What is the contribution of the agricultural sector to GDP? → 15-20%
☛ What is included in the industrial sector? → Manufacturing, Mining, Construction
☛ What does GDP measure? → Total economic activities of a country

सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (GDP) किसी देश की अर्थव्यवस्था के तीन प्रमुख क्षेत्रों - कृषि, उद्योग और सेवा से प्राप्त होता है। ये तीनों क्षेत्र मिलकर देश की कुल आर्थिक गतिविधियों को दर्शाते हैं। कृषि क्षेत्र में फसल उत्पादन, पशुपालन और वानिकी शामिल हैं। औद्योगिक क्षेत्र में विनिर्माण, खनन और निर्माण शामिल हैं, जबकि सेवा क्षेत्र में बैंकिंग, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य और पर्यटन जैसी गतिविधियाँ आती हैं। GDP की गणना इन तीनों क्षेत्रों के योगदान को ध्यान में रखकर की जाती है, जो देश की आर्थिक वृद्धि और विकास को दर्शाता है।

Extra Facts:
GDP की गणना तीन विधियों से की जा सकती है - उत्पादन विधि, आय विधि और व्यय विधि। भारत में, सेवा क्षेत्र का GDP में सबसे बड़ा योगदान होता है, जो लगभग 50% से अधिक है। कृषि क्षेत्र का योगदान घटकर लगभग 15-20% रह गया है, जबकि औद्योगिक क्षेत्र का योगदान लगभग 25-30% है। GDP की वृद्धि दर अर्थव्यवस्था के स्वास्थ्य का एक महत्वपूर्ण संकेतक है।

question:
The GDP estimation method measuring the aggregate value of factor payments is called_______.

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: product method
value added method
expenditure method
income method
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Income Method

Explanation:
The Income Method of GDP estimation measures the aggregate value of all factor payments. This method calculates GDP by summing up all incomes (wages, rent, interest, and profits) generated during production in an economy. It represents the total income paid to factors of production (labor, capital, land, and entrepreneurship). The Income Method is one of the three primary approaches to GDP calculation (Production, Expenditure, and Income) and is a crucial part of national income accounting.

Extra Facts:
The other two methods of GDP calculation are: Production Method (value of total output) and Expenditure Method (total spending). The Income Method includes components of national income such as compensation of employees, corporate profits, rent, etc. All three methods should theoretically yield the same result because, in an economy, total output, total income, and total expenditure are equal.

☛ What does the Production Method measure? → Total output value
☛ What is included in the Expenditure Method? → Consumption, Investment, Government Spending, Net Exports
☛ What is NDP? → GDP - Depreciation

question:
National Income = C (household consumption) + G(____________) + I (investment expense) + NX (net exports).

[SSC GD 2022]
options: household expenditure
individual expenditure
non government expenditure
government expenditure
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is government expenditure

Explanation:
In the formula used to calculate national income, 'G' stands for government expenditure. This represents the spending by the government on public goods and services, such as education, healthcare, defense, and infrastructure. The formula uses the expenditure method to calculate GDP (Gross Domestic Product), which consists of four main components: C (consumption), G (government expenditure), I (investment), and NX (net exports). Government expenditure plays a crucial role in national income as it stimulates economic activity and generates employment.

Extra Facts:
There are three main methods to calculate GDP: production method, income method, and expenditure method. In the expenditure method, GDP = C + G + I + NX. 'C' denotes household consumption, while 'I' represents private investment, such as spending on machinery and buildings. NX is exports minus imports, reflecting the trade balance of a country. Government expenditure (G) includes only spending on final goods and services; transfer payments (like pensions) are not included.

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ How many methods are there to calculate GDP? → Three (Production, Income, Expenditure)
☛ What is the formula for GDP in the expenditure method? → GDP = C + G + I + NX
☛ What does net exports represent? → Exports - Imports
☛ What is not included in government expenditure? → Transfer payments
☛ Which component contributes the most to national income? → Household consumption (C)

question:
Why is it important to distinguish between final and intermediate goods/services in national income accounting?

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: It helps in tracking changes in consumer preferences and market demand.
It helps in more accurate measurement of economic growth and productivity.
Provides insight into the distribution of income among different sectors.
It helps in determining the overall quality of goods and services produced.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It helps in more accurate measurement of economic growth and productivity.

Explanation:
In national income accounting, final goods/services are those consumed by end-users, while intermediate goods/services are used in the production process for further processing. Distinguishing between them is crucial because Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is calculated only on the value of final goods and services. If intermediate goods are included, it leads to double counting, which inflates GDP figures beyond actual economic output. Thus, this distinction ensures accurate measurement of economic growth and productivity by avoiding redundancy in calculations.

Extra Facts:
GDP can be calculated using three methods: Production, Income, and Expenditure. All methods only account for the value of final goods/services. The value of intermediate goods is incorporated through the Value Added approach. Additionally, key economic indicators like Final Consumption Expenditure and Investment are also derived from final goods data. This classification also aids in analyzing sectoral contributions and avoiding statistical distortions in macroeconomic policies.

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ What are the three methods of GDP calculation? → Production, Income, Expenditure
☛ What is double counting? → Including intermediate goods in GDP
☛ Define Value Added method. → Measuring incremental value at each production stage
☛ What is Final Consumption Expenditure? → Spending by end-users on goods/services
☛ Which is excluded from national income accounting? → Non-market activities
question_hi:
राष्ट्रीय आय लेखांकन में अंतिम और मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं/ सेवाओं के बीच अंतर करना क्यों महत्वपूर्ण है?

[SSC MTS 2023]
options_hi: यह उपभोक्ता की प्राथमिकताओं और बाजार की मांग में बदलाव को ट्रैक करने में मदद करता है।
यह आर्थिक विकास और उत्पादकता की अधिक सटीक माप करने में सहायता करता है।
विभिन्न क्षेत्रों के बीच आय के वितरण में अंतर्दृष्टि प्रदान करता है।
यह उत्पादित वस्तुओं और सेवाओं की समग्र गुणवत्ता निर्धारित करने में मदद करता है।
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है यह आर्थिक विकास और उत्पादकता की अधिक सटीक माप करने में सहायता करता है।

Explanation:
राष्ट्रीय आय लेखांकन में अंतिम वस्तुएं/सेवाएं वे होती हैं जो अंतिम उपभोक्ता द्वारा उपयोग की जाती हैं, जबकि मध्यवर्ती वस्तुएं/सेवाएं उत्पादन प्रक्रिया में और प्रसंस्करण के लिए उपयोग की जाती हैं। इनके बीच अंतर करना महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि राष्ट्रीय आय (GDP) की गणना केवल अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं के मूल्य पर की जाती है। यदि मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं को भी शामिल कर लिया जाए, तो दोहरी गणना (Double Counting) की समस्या उत्पन्न हो जाती है, जिससे GDP का आंकड़ा वास्तविकता से अधिक प्रदर्शित होता है। इसलिए, यह अंतर आर्थिक विकास और उत्पादकता को सटीक रूप से मापने में सहायक होता है।

Extra Facts:
GDP (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद) की गणना तीन विधियों से की जा सकती है: उत्पादन विधि, आय विधि और व्यय विधि। इन सभी विधियों में अंतिम वस्तुओं/सेवाओं का ही मूल्य शामिल किया जाता है। मध्यवर्ती वस्तुओं का मूल्य मूल्य वर्धित (Value Added) विधि द्वारा ही गणना में शामिल किया जाता है। इसके अलावा, अंतिम उपभोग व्यय (Final Consumption Expenditure) और निवेश (Investment) जैसे महत्वपूर्ण आर्थिक संकेतकों की गणना भी अंतिम वस्तुओं के आधार पर ही की जाती है।

question:
During the year 1991-92, the industrial production recorded a ______growth of ______.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: negative; 1.1 Percent
positive; 1.1 Percent
negative; 0.9 Percent
positive; 0.6 Percent
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is positive; 0.6 Percent

Explanation:
During the year 1991-92, the Indian economy was undergoing a severe crisis, which led to a slowdown in industrial production. However, industrial production recorded a positive growth of 0.6% during this year. Although the growth was minimal, it was a positive sign despite the crisis. This period marked the beginning of economic reforms (LPG - Liberalization, Privatization, Globalization) in India, which later accelerated industrial growth.

Extra Facts:
During the 1991 economic crisis, India's foreign exchange reserves were nearly depleted, forcing the country to seek assistance from the IMF. Post-crisis, the New Economic Policy (NEP) was implemented, promoting liberalization, privatization, and globalization. Despite slow industrial growth, these reforms laid the foundation for future economic progress.

question:
Which of the following is NOT a part of aggregate demand in an economy?

[RRC GROUP D]
options: Exports
Increase in population
Capital goods
Imports
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Increase in population

Explanation:
Aggregate Demand (AD) represents the total demand for final goods and services in an economy and consists of four components: Consumption Expenditure (C), Investment Expenditure (I), Government Expenditure (G), and Net Exports (NX = Exports - Imports). Increase in population is a demographic factor that may indirectly influence AD but is not a direct component of AD. In contrast, exports and capital goods (part of investment) are AD components, while imports are subtracted in NX.

Extra Facts:
The AD curve shows a negative relationship between price level and real GDP. According to Keynesian economics, shifts in AD affect short-run output. The interest rate effect, real wealth effect, and foreign trade effect explain its downward slope. While population growth may boost labor supply and potential GDP in the long run, it is not a direct AD component.

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ What is the formula for Aggregate Demand? → AD = C + I + G + (X - M)
☛ How is the slope of the AD curve? → Downward sloping
☛ What is the core principle of Keynesian economics? → Demand drives short-run output
☛ What are net exports? → Exports - Imports
☛ Which AD component includes government spending? → G
question_hi:
निम्न में से कौन सा किसी अर्थव्यवस्था में समग्र मांग का भाग नहीं है?

[RRC GROUP D]
options_hi: निर्यात
जनसंख्या वृद्धि
पूंजीगत माल
आयात
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है जनसंख्या वृद्धि

Explanation:
समग्र मांग (Aggregate Demand - AD) एक अर्थव्यवस्था में सभी अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं की मांग का कुल योग है। यह चार मुख्य घटकों से बनी होती है: उपभोग व्यय (C), निवेश व्यय (I), सरकारी व्यय (G), और शुद्ध निर्यात (NX = निर्यात - आयात)। जनसंख्या वृद्धि एक जनसांख्यिकीय कारक है जो अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से AD को प्रभावित कर सकता है, लेकिन यह स्वयं AD का घटक नहीं है। इसके विपरीत, निर्यात और पूंजीगत माल (निवेश का हिस्सा) AD के घटक हैं, जबकि आयात NX में घटाव के रूप में शामिल होता है।

Extra Facts:
समग्र मांग वक्र (AD Curve) कीमत स्तर और वास्तविक GDP के बीच एक ऋणात्मक संबंध दिखाता है। कीन्सियन अर्थशास्त्र के अनुसार, AD में परिवर्तन अल्पकाल में आर्थिक उत्पादन को प्रभावित करते हैं। ब्याज दर प्रभाव, वास्तविक संपत्ति प्रभाव, और विदेशी व्यापार प्रभाव AD वक्र के ढलान को समझाते हैं। जनसंख्या वृद्धि दीर्घकाल में श्रम आपूर्ति और संभावित GDP को बढ़ा सकती है, लेकिन यह AD का सीधा घटक नहीं है।

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :

☛ AD वक्र का ढलान कैसा होता है? → नीचे की ओर
☛ कीन्सियन अर्थशास्त्र का मुख्य सिद्धांत क्या है? → अल्पकाल में मांग महत्वपूर्ण
